**1. What is the scholarship information?**

Yes! SPUS offers several scholarship and financial assistance programs:

- **Academic and Athletic Scholarships**: Available for qualified college and high school students based on academic standing or sports excellence. Visit the Guidance Office for application guidelines.
- **ESC Grants**: 350 Educational Service Contracting (ESC) slots for incoming Grade 7 junior high students.
- **Senior High Voucher Program**: Tuition subsidy for incoming Grade 11 students (automatically granted to public school completers; ESC certificate required for private junior high completers).
- **Student on Study Assistance Program (SSAP)**: Work-study financial grant program administered by the Scholarship Coordinator / SSAP Office.

For inquiries and application forms, visit the **Guidance Office** or consult the Scholarship Coordinator.

Yes! SPUS offers several scholarship and financial assistance programs:

- **Academic and Athletic Scholarships**: Available for qualified college and high school students based on academic standing or sports excellence. Visit the Guidance Office for application guidelines.
- **ESC Grants**: 350 Educational Service Contracting (ESC) slots for incoming Grade 7 junior high students.
- **Senior High Voucher Program**: Tuition subsidy for incoming Grade 11 students (automatically granted to public school completers; ESC certificate required for private junior high completers).
- **Student on Study Assistance Program (SSAP)**: Work-study financial grant program administered by the Scholarship Coordinator / SSAP Office.

For inquiries and application forms, visit the **Guidance Office** or consult the Scholarship Coordinator.

HISTORY OF THE SISTERS OF ST. PAUL OF CHARTRES
The Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres (SPC) community was founded in 1696 by Fr. Louis Chauvet, parish priest of Levesville-La Chenard, a small village southeast of Chartres, France.

The 17th century was a time of great change and unrest for France and the rest of the world that went through the Hundred Years War. Levesville experienced the effects of the previous wars. The country was ruined. The people were burdened with both material and spiritual needs. While the education of the elite had reached an excellent level, the ignorance, apathy and illiteracy of the poor grew increasingly alarming.

Aware of the conditions of their time, Fr. Chauvet felt the need to offer instruction to the poor children of Levesville. He "wanted them to study, to learn more about Christian doctrine, to participate more fully and intimately in religious ceremonies, and to practice religion truly and perfectly." Father Chauvet's vision of charity was shared by his first followers: Marie Micheau, Barbe Foucault, and Marie Therese du Tronchay. Fr. Chauvet entrusted their training to Marie Anne de Tilly, a lady of nobility and an active member of the parish who left a life of comfort "to serve God and neighbor".

INTERVENTIONS
Interventions are therapeutic programs appropriate for high-risk individuals and students who are using dangerous drugs and who need special assistance to recognize the signs and symptoms of initial drug use and dependency. It may include corrective or rehabilitative actions that may take the form of crisis intervention, peer counseling at the individual or family level, and structured rehabilitation programs. It may also include medical intervention of the afflicted student whenever necessary. Four (4) major modalities of Intervention that can be given, as established by the Department of Health (DOH) are: (1) in-patient, (2) out-patient, (3) recovery homes/half-way houses, and (4) community-based interventions.

INSTRUMENT
Anything that is used in or intended to be used in any manner in the commission of illegal drug trafficking or related offenses.

MANDATORY DRUG TESTING
Refers to the compulsory submission of a student for drug testing as required in the school's student handbook and with notice to the parents.

MANDATORY RANDOM DRUG TESTING
Refers to the compulsory conduct of random drug testing of students in all HEIs with each student having an equal chance of being selected for testing.

SCREENING DRUG TEST
Refers to a rapid test performed to establish potential or presumptive positive result. It refers to the immunoassay test to eliminate a negative specimen, i.e., one without the presence of dangerous drugs from further consideration and to identify the presumptively positive specimen that requires confirmatory test.

SALE
Any act of giving away any dangerous drug and/or controlled precursor and essential chemical whether for money or any other consideration.

The National Discipline Awards program was established in 1990 in response to Ambassador Alfonso T. Yuchengco's call to instill national discipline in the country's youth. Since its inception, the award has been conferred on more than 13,000 high school and senior high school graduates from more than 1,200 partner schools nationwide. Although not a scholarship program, the National Discipline Award encourages awardees to pursue their studies. Thus, together with the San Lorenzo Ruiz gold medal, Rhea Mula received a cash award of PhP 7,500.00 as an aid to her college tuition. Since 2014, Mula is the fourth Paulinian to receive the AY Foundation National Discipline Award.

The National Discipline Awards program was established in 1990 in response to Ambassador Alfonso T. Yuchengco's call to instill national discipline in the country's youth. Since its inception, the award has been conferred on more than 13,000 high school and senior high school graduates from more than 1,200 partner schools nationwide. Although not a scholarship program, the National Discipline Award encourages awardees to pursue their studies. Thus, together with the San Lorenzo Ruiz gold medal, Rhea Mula received a cash award of PhP 7,500.00 as an aid to her college tuition. Since 2014, Mula is the fourth Paulinian to receive the AY Foundation National Discipline Award.

During the lecture, Rep. Elago gave examples on how to lead amidst the pandemic, such as maximizing the use of available social platforms. LAUREL LEAF
It signifies glory through academic excellence and divine approval, which the Paulinian seeks to achieve, especially of a life well-lived in service of others. It is a reminder of the Christocentric paschal spirituality and challenges every Paulinian to accept and endure the pains that are our share in the sufferings of Christ so we could share in His victory. In early times, it symbolized the palm of martyrdom for those who died for the faith.

WAVY LINE
It signifies the waters of the sea that connotes readiness to go where mission calls and the tranquil daring to face what is difficult and unknown. It is a symbol of a missionary life of the Paulinian who is willing to go through life preaching and witnessing to Christ.

is chaired by the Finance Executive Officer, with the other Executive Officers as members. SECTION 8. STUDENT ON STUDY ASSISTANCE PROGRAM (SSAP)
8.1 Conditions for SSAP Enrolment and Duty Hours Schedule
    8.1.1 SSAP grantee shall present previous grades of the semester to the SSAP Head. SSAP grantee shall have no grade below 80 in every semester and must obtain a performance rating of 3 on a scale of 1-5.
    8.1.2 SSAP grantee must schedule duty hours in such a way that 2 duty hours daily will be spent during the day.
    8.1.3 SSAP grantee shall present class and duty schedules to SSAP Head and Immediate Head for approval.
    8.1.4 SSAP grantee can take Education courses and BUS as priority.
    8.1.5 Exemptions of the above conditions will be upon the discretion of the Administration of the University.

About us
The Saint Paul University Surigao, also referred to as SPUS or SPU Surigao, is a private, Catholic basic and higher education institution run by the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres (SPC) in Surigao City, Surigao del Norte, Philippines.

It has two campuses: the main campus in the heart of Surigao City houses the college academic units, graduate school and offices and the satellite campus at Brgy. Luna which houses the high school and grade school.

SPUS is the first university in the Caraga region and is identified as the center for development in teacher education and the regional center for Gender and Development, it being the seat of CARAGA Women's resources center established in 1906.

It is one of the seven campuses comprising the St. Paul University System.

It is one of the 40 schools owned, managed, and operated by the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres (SPC) in the Philippines.

St. Paul University Surigao traces its roots to the year 1906 when the last group of Spanish Benedictine Missionaries, who had worked zealously as founders of the Cartilla or Doctrina School (which soon evolved into Escuela Catolica de San Nicolas), with the Religious of the Virgin Mary as administrators, vacated Surigao. Soon after their departure, the Missionaries of the Sacred Heart, also known as the Dutch Fathers, succeeded them, created the parish of Surigao, and made Escuela Catolica de San Nicolas a parochial school which they renamed San Nicolas School.

**1. What Graduate School programs does SPUS offer?**

GRADUATE SCHOOL
Graduate School and Professional Studies
VISION
A center of excellence in the graduate programs of business, pedagogy, health sciences, and arts.
OBJECTIVES
Develop outstanding Christian leaders and experts who are imbued with integrity, public accountability, and a deep sense of commitment to help improve the quality of life in the local and global communities.
Encourage and promote productive, functional research in all fields of endeavor.
Upgrade the discipline-specific competencies of professionals and enable them to lead productive academic and professional lives in the academe, the public sector, or private industry.
Develop qualified individuals who can engage in scholarly inquiry and communications.
Integrate theory and practice in teaching, supervision, administration, and management and thereby contribute to human society, cultural heritage, and the natural environment.
GSPS Attributes
ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE
Show expertise in the competencies necessary to the practice of the profession.
LEADERSHIP and TEAMWORK
Demonstrate capacity for leadership and teamwork including the ability to motivate others to be responsible and reliable.
CRITICAL THINKING, RESEARCH AND PROBLEM-SOLVING SKILLS
Initiate innovative ideas and methods through research responsive to the changing needs of society.
PRODUCTIVITY and ACCOUNTABILITY
Develop new knowledge and understanding that will contribute to nation-building and sustainable development through the process of inquiry, research, and innovation.
SOCIAL and ETHICAL RESPONSIBILITY
Uphold Catholic values and moral principles reflective of a Paulinian in the formation of humanely progressive and healthy society.
COMMUNICATION and RELATIONAL SKILLS
Develop effective communication competencies through interpersonal skills, and utilize information technology responsibly as an effective tool in exploring and expressing ideas.

Graduate School Programs
Programs Offered
Doctor of Philosophy in Educational Management
Doctor of Philosophy in Business and Management
Master of Business Administration
Master of Public Administration
Master of Science in Nursing
Master of Arts in Nursing
Master of Arts in Science Teaching
Master of Arts in Mathematics Teaching
Master of Arts in English
Master of Arts in Filipino
Master of Arts in Home Economics
Master of Arts in Cultural Education
Master of Arts in Curriculum Development and Design

College of Health Sciences Program
The College of Health Sciences is committed to excellence in education, research, and service in the fields of healthcare and behavioral sciences. It offers the Bachelor of Science in Nursing, designed to develop highly skilled and compassionate nursing professionals, and the Bachelor of Science in Psychology, which prepares students for meaningful roles in mental health, research, and human development. Guided by a strong foundation of scientific knowledge, ethical practice, and social responsibility, the College of Health Sciences equips graduates to respond to the growing demands of healthcare and to contribute significantly to the well-being of individuals and communities.

Data Privacy Policy
St. Paul University Surigao is committed to protecting the privacy and personal data of its students, faculty, staff, and other individuals associated with the university. This Data Privacy Policy outlines how the university collects, uses, discloses, and safeguards personal information in accordance with the applicable data protection laws and regulations.

Collection and Use of Personal Information
St. Paul University Surigao collects personal information directly from individuals for purposes related to education, employment, administration, and other university-related activities. This may include information such as names, contact details, identification numbers, academic records, employment history, and other relevant data.
The university collects personal information solely for lawful and legitimate purposes, including but not limited to admissions, academic services, human resources, payroll, alumni relations, security, research, and statistical analysis.
Personal information may be used to communicate important updates, provide academic and administrative support, facilitate transactions, ensure campus security, and improve the overall educational experience.
Data Disclosure and Sharing
St. Paul University Surigao may share personal information with third parties only when necessary and with appropriate safeguards in place. This may include government authorities, regulatory bodies, service providers, research partners, educational institutions, and other trusted entities.
Personal information will not be disclosed, sold, or rented to unauthorized third parties for marketing or commercial purposes without the individual’s explicit consent.
Data Retention and Security
Personal information will be retained for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected, comply with legal obligations, or as required by the university’s policies and procedures.
St. Paul University Surigao takes appropriate technical, organizational, and physical measures to protect personal information against unauthorized access, loss, theft, or misuse. These measures include but are not limited to firewalls, encryption, access controls, staff training, and regular system audits.
In the event of a data breach, the university will promptly investigate, mitigate the impact, and notify the affected individuals and relevant authorities as required by law.
Individual Rights
Individuals have the right to access, correct, update, or request the deletion of their personal information, subject to any applicable legal restrictions or university policies.
Requests related to personal data should be submitted in writing to the university’s designated Data Privacy Officer (DPO), whose contact information will be made available to all individuals.
The university will respond to data subject requests in a timely and appropriate manner, ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
Data Privacy Awareness and Compliance
St. Paul University Surigao is committed to promoting awareness and understanding of data privacy among its employees, students, and relevant stakeholders. Training programs and information sessions will be conducted to ensure compliance with this policy and applicable data protection laws.
The university will regularly review and update its data privacy practices and policies to align with evolving legal and regulatory requirements and best practices.
By using the services and facilities provided by St. Paul University Surigao, individuals acknowledge their understanding and acceptance of this Data Privacy Policy.

rows.query: [PBMO] What is the SPUS Policy on Online Posting (Document PBMO-PO-010 / PBMO-PR-009)?
rows.normalized: [PBMO] What is the SPUS Policy on Online Posting (Document PBMO-PO-010 / PBMO-PR-009)?
rows.reply:
Sige—narito ang impormasyon mula sa mga nakaimbak na sanggunian.

The SPUS Policy on Online Posting (PBMO-PO-010) governs all digital postings on the university's official online platforms:
1. Authority: PBMO oversees and coordinates all online postings on the official institutional webpage and social media channels.
2. Timeliness: Updates, announcements, and news items should be posted promptly, ideally not later than 2 days after the event. Audio-Visual Presentations (AVPs) may be released later if an initial event post has already been published.
3. Content Criteria: Must align with SPUS mission, vision, and Gospel values, remain accurate and free of misinformation, and uphold respect for diversity and inclusion.
4. Permitted Activities: Academic achievements, official administrative announcements, upcoming events/seminars/workshops, community outreach/social responsibility, and student organization activities.
5. Visual Content: Must comply with copyright laws, respect individual dignity, and adhere to official SPUS graphic and branding standards.

rows.reply:
Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

The 4 steps for publishing materials online through PBMO (PBMO-PR-009):
1. Step 1 (Unit Personnel): Submits a formal request for documentation or laying out of publication materials (via letter, email, or communication).
2. Step 2 (Web, Layout and Marketing Staff / School Paper Layout Artists): Prepares the layout and draft of the publication material.
3. Step 3 (PBMO Director): Reviews and approves the final publication material.
4. Step 4 (PBMO Director & Page Administrator): Publishes the approved material onto the official university online platforms.

rows.query: [PBMO] What are the official colors and brand palette of St. Paul University Surigao (SPUS)?
rows.normalized: [PBMO] What are the official colors and brand palette of St. Paul University Surigao (SPUS)?
rows.reply:
Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

The official SPUS Brand Color Palette consists of:
- Primary Colors: Paulinian Green (#005301 / #002c04 / #215a2e) and Paulinian Gold/Yellow (#deb402 / #fcd108). Primary colors are mandatory for official logos, letterheads, diplomas, certificates, signage, and banners.
- Secondary Colors: Supporting accents used to complement (never replace) the primary palette in backgrounds, callouts, and highlighters, including deep blue (#0101c1) and accent red (#da0200).
- Typography: Primary font for headlines/titles and secondary font for body text. Fonts must never be stretched, compressed, or distorted.

The official SPUS Brand Color Palette consists of:
- Primary Colors: Paulinian Green (#005301 / #002c04 / #215a2e) and Paulinian Gold/Yellow (#deb402 / #fcd108). Primary colors are mandatory for official logos, letterheads, diplomas, certificates, signage, and banners.
- Secondary Colors: Supporting accents used to complement (never replace) the primary palette in backgrounds, callouts, and highlighters, including deep blue (#0101c1) and accent red (#da0200).
- Typography: Primary font for headlines/titles and secondary font for body text. Fonts must never be stretched, compressed, or distorted.

Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

The SPUS University Seal embodies the university's Paulinian identity and heritage:
- University Motto: Caritas (Charity), Veritas (Truth), Scientia (Science/Knowledge).
- Foundation Year: 1906 (established in Surigao City as the first university in the Caraga Region).
- Patron: St. Paul the Apostle; Model: Mary, Mother of God.
- Charism: Guided by the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres (SPC), forming Christ-centered, integrated, competent, and responsible persons in the service of Church and society.

rows.query: [Registrar] What is the procedure for Changing, Adding, Dropping, or Withdrawing subjects (Document URO-PR-007)?
rows.normalized: [Registrar] What is the procedure for Changing, Adding, Dropping, or Withdrawing subjects (Document URO-PR-007)?
rows.reply:
Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

The official University Registrar procedure for Changing, Adding, Dropping, or Withdrawal of Subjects (URO-PR-007) applies to all officially enrolled students in basic and higher education:
1. Step 1 (Student): Requests a Changing/Adding/Dropping/Withdrawal form from the Registrar's Clerk.
2. Step 2 (Clerk): Issues the official Request for Changing/Adding/Dropping/Withdrawal form.
3. Step 3 (Student): Fills out the form completely with subject codes, descriptions, and valid reasons.
4. Step 4 (Approvals): Secures required approval signatures from the Dean, Subject Teacher/STL, University Registrar, and Vice President for Finance Services.
5. Step 5 (Student): Furnishes final signed copies to the Finance Office and the University Registrar's Office to record and finalize the adjustment.

[SUGGESTIONS: "Who must approve the subject adding, dropping, or withdrawal form?" | "What are the required documents for transferee students enrolling at SPUS?" | "Where is the registrar office?"]

rows.normalized: [Registrar] What is the procedure for Changing, Adding, Dropping, or withdrawing subjects (Document URO-PR-007)?
rows.reply:
Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

The official University Registrar procedure for Changing, Adding, Dropping, or Withdrawal of Subjects (URO-PR-007) applies to all officially enrolled students in basic and higher education:
1. Step 1 (Student): Requests a Changing/Adding/Dropping/Withdrawal form from the Registrar's Clerk.
2. Step 2 (Clerk): Issues the official Request for Changing/Adding/Dropping/Withdrawal form.
3. Step 3 (Student): Fills out the form completely with subject codes, descriptions, and valid reasons.
4. Step 4 (Approvals): Secures required approval signatures from the Dean, Subject Teacher/STL, University Registrar, and Vice President for Finance Services.
5. Step 5 (Student): Furnishes final signed copies to the Finance Office and the University Registrar's Office to record and finalize the adjustment.

Requirements for Transferee Students in Higher Education:
1. Official Transfer Credentials (Honorable Dismissal / Transcript of Records for evaluation)
2. Curricular Checklist from previous school
3. Original PSA Birth Certificate
4. Original Certificate of Good Moral Character
5. 1 pc. 2x2 ID picture
6. Accomplished Student Information Sheet (at SAO)

rows.query: [Registrar] What are the required admission and enrollment documents for incoming freshmen at SPUS?
rows.normalized: [Registrar] What are the required admission and enrollment documents for incoming freshmen at SPUS? (incoming college freshmen)
rows.reply:
Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

Admission and enrollment requirements for Incoming College Freshmen:
1. Senior High School (SHS) Report Card (Form 138 / SF9)
2. Original PSA Birth Certificate
3. Original Certificate of Good Moral Character
4. College Entrance Examination Result (from Guidance Office)
5. 1 pc. 2x2 ID picture
6. Marriage Certificate (if married)
7. Accomplished Student Information Sheet

rows.reply:
Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

The Changing, Adding, Dropping, or Withdrawal of Subjects form (URO-PR-007) requires approval signatures from:
1. College Dean
2. Subject Teacher / Subject Team Leader (STL)
3. University Registrar
4. Vice President for Finance Services

Once signed, the student must furnish copies to both the Finance Office and the Registrar's Office.

- Start of Classes (August)
- Preliminary Examinations
- Midterm Examinations
- University Foundation Day / Paulinian Week (November)
- Final Examinations
- Christmas Break (December)

**Second Semester (January – May)**
- Enrollment Period (January)
- Start of Classes (January)
- Preliminary Examinations
- Midterm Examinations
- Lenten/Holy Week Break (March/April)
- Final Examinations
- Baccalaureate Mass & Commencement Exercises (May)

**Key Annual Events & Activities:**
- Feast of the Conversion of St. Paul (January 25)
- Paulinian Week / Foundation Day Celebration
- Intramurals / Sports Festival
- Academic & Cultural Competitions
- Community Extension Programs
- Recognition & Awards Ceremony
- Commencement Exercises / Graduation

For the exact dates and detailed schedule of the current academic year, please visit the SPUS Official Website at https://spus.edu.ph or inquire at the Registrar's Office.

PAULINIAN CORE VALUES
Charism
The Paulinian develops his or her gifts or talents to be put in the service of the community, he or she strives to grow and improve daily, always seeking the better and finer things, and the final good.
Christ-Centered
Christ is the center of Paulinian life; he or she follows and imitates Christ, doing everything in reference to Him.
Commission
The Paulinian has a mission – a life purpose to spread the Good News; like Christ, he/she actively works “to save” this world, to make it better place to live in.
Community
The Paulinian is a responsible family member and citizen, concerned with building communities, promotion of people, justice, and peace, and the protection of the environment.
Charity
Urged on by the love of Christ, the Paulinian is warm, hospitable, and “all to all”, especially to the underprivileged.

rows.query: [About SPUS.txt] What is the early history of SPUS?
rows.normalized: [About SPUS.txt] What is the early history of SPUS?
rows.reply:
Sure—here is the information from the stored sources.

St. Paul University Surigao traces its roots to the year 1906 when the last group of Spanish Benedictine Missionaries, who had worked zealously as founders of the Cartilla or Doctrina School (which soon evolved into Escuela Catolica de San Nicolas), with the Religious of the Virgin Mary as administrators, vacated Surigao. Soon after their departure, the Missionaries of the Sacred Heart, also known as the Dutch Fathers, succeeded them, created the parish of Surigao, and made Escuela Catolica de San Nicolas a parochial school which they renamed San Nicolas School.

- Bachelor of Arts (Major in: Political Science, Philosophy, English Language, Sociology, Mass Communication)
- Bachelor of Science in Mathematics
- Bachelor of Science in Public Administration
- Bachelor of Elementary Education
- Bachelor of Secondary Education (Major in: English, Filipino, Mathematics, Sciences, Social Studies, Values Education)
- Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
- Bachelor of Physical Education

**College of Business Management and Accountancy (4-Year Curriculum)**
- Bachelor of Science in Accountancy
- Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (Major in: Financial Management, Marketing Management, Human Resource Development Management)
- Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management
- Bachelor of Science in Tourism Management
- Bachelor of Science in Accounting and Information System
- Bachelor of Science in Office Administration

**College of Engineering & Information Technology (4-Year Curriculum)**
- Bachelor of Science in Mining Engineering
- Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
- Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
- Bachelor of Science in Information Technology

**College of Criminal Justice Education (4-Year Curriculum)**
- Bachelor of Science in Criminology
- Bachelor of Forensic Science

Choosing SPUS means embracing:
- Faith-Based Education: Integrating Catholic Christian values and Paulinian spirituality forming ethically grounded, compassionate, and Christ-centered leaders.
- Academic Excellence: An Outcomes-Based Education (OBE) framework delivered by expert faculty ensuring rigorous academics and industry-relevant skills for success in today's global economy.
- Vibrant Campus Life: Diverse student organizations, engaging campus events, and opportunities for service and holistic personal growth.
- Global Alumni Network: A vast, interconnected community of competent and compassionate Paulinian graduates worldwide, offering mentorship, professional connections, and lifelong support.
